Terrible experience. I took my cat, who was having trouble eating, to the vet to run tests and make money, when she could have just been sedated. They couldn't find the cause because there was nothing to justify it in the abdominal ultrasound or in her mouth except for two missing teeth (only a huge lump seen by another vet). They wanted to insert a feeding tube because she wasn't eating until she started eating again, without doing any further tests. Obviously, she wasn't going to come back because she couldn't. I didn't keep her hospitalized; she was stressed with a Labrador barking at her in the cage next door. I took her to other vets and fed her with a syringe until they discovered the cause. It was a tumor on her head, which led to facial paralysis. Even though I told them she had chronic otitis, they ignored it because her ears were clean. In other words, it was pointless for me to inform them that she couldn't eat and had otitis because they ignored it. The solution? To give her medication to stimulate her appetite and then judge me for not keeping her hospitalized. I don't recommend them to anyone.
